_comment: The public address of every deployed Worker, per environment. ONE source of
truth, read by .github/scripts/verify-deploy.sh and by
services/api/test/db-identity.test.ts.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Both of those hardcoded a workers.dev hostname pattern.
On 16 Aug 2026 the api.marginsheet.com route was added to wrangler.jsonc,
Cloudflare disabled the workers.dev hostname for that Worker as it does
whenever explicit routes are declared, and two blocking checks went red
against an address nobody reaches while production itself was healthy.
The asymmetry below is deliberate and correct: production has a custom
domain because households reach it, and dev and staging do not because
nobody does. A check should verify the address households actually use, not
a pattern that happens to be true today. When an address changes, change it
here and the checks follow it instead of going red.
AMENDED 19 Aug 2026, AND THE ASYMMETRY BELOW IS A TRANSITION, NOT A DESIGN.
conversation was reached at a workers.dev address, which worked only because
the Worker was publicly reachable, and it should never have been. Closing that
turned db-identity red, which is the correct order of events: the check was
depending on the gap.
dev and staging are already private and are reached THROUGH api over a service
binding. production is still direct because api's proxy route does not exist
there until this merges and deploys. The follow-up privatises production
conversation and moves it to `via`, at which point every environment matches.
Tracked as retract-workers-dev-staging-production in docs/open-items.json.
